back_translation: Cast your bread upon the surface of the waters, for after many days you will find it again.
Give your portion to seven, or even to eight, for you do not know what disaster may come upon the land.
If the clouds are full of rain, they will pour it out on the earth; whether a tree falls to the south or to the north, wherever it falls, there it lies.
He who keeps watching the wind will not sow, and he who keeps looking at the clouds will not reap.
Just as you do not know the way of the wind, or how the bones take form in the mother's womb, so you cannot know the work of God who makes all things.
Sow your seed in the morning, and do not let your hand rest in the evening, for you do not know which work will succeed — this one or that one — or whether both alike will be good.
Light is sweet, and it is pleasing to the eyes to see the sun.
So if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all; but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many. Everything that is to come is without substance.

Rejoice, O young man, in your youth, and let your heart be glad in the days of your young manhood. Walk in the ways of your heart and in what your eyes see — but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
Banish sorrow from your heart and put away pain from your body, for youth and the dawn of life are without substance.
